_what: The flow take for the ore plant: which filter is shown when, where each station is filmed from, and what a train-load consists of. Lived in tools/mk-flow-take.mjs as tables in the source until the studio needed to edit them. tools/mk-flow-take.mjs reads this and writes the take.
_stations: A station is named by literal block coordinates rather than by a part name: a part is everything an assembly owns, and half of that is housing the shot does not want in frame. A station with a bearing is filmed from outside, arcing in; one with an inside range is filmed from within the plant, which is the only way to read the crusher at all.

framing._arc: Subtracted from a station's bearing so the *final* frame lands on the bearing asked for, rather than starting there and swinging past it.
framing._idealDistance: The closest air to a funnel buried in a plant is usually the block directly above it, and a shot looking straight down tells a viewer nothing about which funnel it is — the first cut of this beat had nine of the twenty-two at a pitch of ninety. So a steep angle is paid for, and so is standing too close or too far to read the thing.

stations.name: dock
stations.what: the chest the train unloads into, and the two chutes under it

stations.name: crusher
stations.what: two wheels, the controller between them, and the belt that carries the crushed ore out

stations.name: washer
stations.what: the fan, the waterlogged leaf in front of it, and what comes off the belt below

stations.name: press
stations.what: three basins with a press over each, and the funnels that feed them off the lanes

_filters: Gone, deliberately. A filter is set when its funnel is put down, not in a second pass over the finished plant — so the build take dwells on the block and opens it there. The positions come out of schematics/ore_plant.groups.json, which tools/parts.py fills in from the block entities.
